sources.title: Information for those who visit San Marino
sources.publisher: Department of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of San Marino
sources.officialityEvidence: San Marino's Foreign Affairs Department directly requires visitors to hold the necessary Schengen entry and transit authorisations before departure and states the 30-day local threshold.
sources.supportingExcerpt: To reach the Republic of San Marino it is necessary to transit through the Schengen area.

sources.title: Consolidated rules on entry and stay of foreigners, updated 9 April 2024
sources.officialityEvidence: The official Foreign Affairs legal index publishes the consolidated foreign-entry law. Article 5 requires a valid passport and, where applicable, the Schengen visa for entry or transit.
sources.supportingExcerpt: lo straniero ... deve essere in possesso, se richiesto, di visto in corso di validità

sources.title: Countries exempt from short-stay visas
sources.publisher: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.officialityEvidence: Italy's MFA maintains the current official short-stay exemption schedule for ordinary passports, with the biometric, Serbian Coordination Directorate and Taiwan conditions stated on the page.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Nationals of the following countries ... are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of up to 90 days.

sources.title: Countries whose citizens need a visa to cross the border
sources.publisher: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.officialityEvidence: Italy's MFA publishes the current ordinary-passport countries subject to the Schengen visa obligation, expressly tying the schedule to Regulation (EU) 2018/1806.
sources.supportingExcerpt: I cittadini ... titolari di passaporto ordinario, sono soggetti o meno ad obbligo di visto Schengen.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, consolidated 30 December 2025
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex hosts the current consolidated Regulation. Articles 3–4 and Annexes I–II set the legal short-stay split; Nauru's Annex II footnote makes its waiver conditional on an agreement entering into force.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Nationals of third countries listed in Annex I shall be required to be in possession of a visa.

sources.title: EU visa agreements with non-EU countries
sources.officialityEvidence: The Council's official visa-agreements register was reviewed on 3 March 2026. Its Nauru note confirms the conditional visa-free regime has not begun because the waiver agreement is not concluded.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Visa-free regime will apply only once Nauru and EU have concluded a visa waiver agreement.

sources.title: Directive 2004/38/EC: right of entry for Union citizens
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex publishes the EU free-movement directive. Article 5 establishes the no-entry-visa rule for Union citizens entering a Member State with a valid identity card or passport.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No entry visa or equivalent formality may be imposed on Union citizens.

sources.title: Schengen Borders Code: persons with equivalent free-movement rights
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex hosts the consolidated Schengen Borders Code. Its free-movement definition includes third-country nationals with equivalent rights under Union and Member-State agreements.
sources.supportingExcerpt: third-country nationals ... enjoy rights of free movement equivalent to those of Union citizens

sources.title: General conditions for entry of foreign nationals into Italy
sources.publisher: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.officialityEvidence: Italy's MFA describes the current Schengen/Italian entry conditions, including passport, purpose, means, visa where prescribed and the separate short-stay residence-permit exception.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Lo straniero già residente in uno Stato Schengen e titolare di permesso di soggiorno, è esente da visto.

sources.title: Italian entry visa
sources.publisher: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.officialityEvidence: Italy's MFA describes the current Schengen visa as a sticker in a passport or valid travel document, distinguishing consular visa issuance from electronic application availability.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Il visto ... consta di un'apposita vignetta ... applicata sul passaporto.

sources.title: European Travel Information and Authorisation System: current status
sources.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Migration and Home Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The European Commission's Smart Borders page reports the current operational status of ETIAS, the planned electronic authorisation for visa-exempt travellers.
sources.supportingExcerpt: ETIAS is currently not in operation and no applications for travel authorisations are collected at this point.

sources.title: Civil-status and passport service charter, April 2026
sources.publisher: Government of the Republic of San Marino, Civil Status Office
sources.officialityEvidence: San Marino's current April 2026 Civil Status service charter states that its passport holder must be a Sammarinese citizen and describes ordinary passport issuance.
sources.supportingExcerpt: IL TITOLARE DEVE ESSERE CITTADINO SAMMARINESE.

policies.title: Sammarinese ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A Sammarinese national travelling on a Sammarinese ordinary passport is classified as citizenship rather than as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: The current passport-service charter limits the holder to a Sammarinese citizen. This is a citizenship classification, not a foreign-visitor visa rule.
It does not define entry by a dual national presenting another passport, residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: visa-free visitor access via Italy
policies.summary: San Marino has no separate entry visa for a visitor who is compliant with Schengen access through Italy. Union citizens do not need an entry visa for that access leg.
conditions: This records the ordinary-passport short-visitor route via Italy, not membership of San Marino in Schengen.
San Marino Foreign Affairs says a stay exceeding 30 days requires a stay permit or residence. Carry a valid passport or equivalent identity document.
No San Marino eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival is established.

policies.title: Visa-exempt Schengen-access ordinary passports: visa-free visitor access
policies.summary: A visitor with these qualifying passports is compliant with the Italian Schengen access rule and may visit San Marino without a separate San Marino entry visa.
conditions: San Marino requires the necessary Schengen entry and transit authorisations before departure; a stay exceeding 30 days requires a stay permit or residence.

Biometric passport is required for AL, BA, GE, MK, MD, ME, RS, UA and XK. The Italian MFA schedule excludes Serbian Coordination Directorate passports; Taiwan requires the identity-card number; HK and MO require their named SAR passports.
CH, IS, LI and NO follow equivalent free-movement treatment for the Italian access leg; this does not make San Marino part of Schengen.

ETIAS is not operating on the research date. Schengen residence-permit and family-status routes are document-conditioned exceptions outside this passport-code baseline, as are special passport and refugee-document rules.
Minor-specific identity, parental-authorisation and carrier or Italian controls are outside this adult ordinary-passport classification.

policies.title: Schengen-visa-required ordinary passports: visitor access via Italy
policies.summary: These ordinary passports require the Italian/Schengen visa needed for access through Italy; San Marino does not issue a separate entry visa.
conditions: This is the advance Schengen visa required for entry through Italy, not a separate San Marino visa. The Italian MFA describes a visa sticker affixed to the passport or other travel document; no eVisa status is established.
San Marino requires the necessary Schengen authorisation before departure; a local stay exceeding 30 days requires a stay permit or residence.

Italian entry conditions separately require a valid travel document, purpose and means evidence, a visa where prescribed, and no refusal/security ground. A Schengen residence permit holder has a separately stated 90-in-180 visa exemption; that document-conditioned route does not change this ordinary-passport nationality baseline.
Minor, diplomatic/official/service, refugee/stateless, residence, work, transit and other special-document exceptions are not flattened into this policy.

application.label: Italian MFA entry-visa information
application.processingTime: The cited page does not publish a universal decision-time promise; consult the competent Italian consular post for the itinerary and residence location.
steps: Apply through the competent Italian consular channel for the Schengen access itinerary.
Obtain the Schengen visa sticker in the valid travel document before travelling to Italy and onward to San Marino.
Present the visa, passport and supporting entry documents for Italian border control; carry identity documentation in San Marino.

policies.title: Nauru ordinary passport: Schengen visa required pending EU waiver
policies.summary: Nauru's Annex II exemption is conditional on entry into force of an EU waiver agreement. The current Council register says visa-free travel applies only once Nauru and the EU conclude that agreement, so the route through Italy remains visa required.
conditions: This is the Schengen visa needed for Italian entry before visiting San Marino; a local stay exceeding 30 days requires a stay permit or residence.
Do not classify Nauru as visa-free until an official source confirms the EU–Nauru waiver agreement is concluded and in force.
No San Marino eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established.
